title: What If the Entire Greenland Ice Sheet Melted?

scenes.text: What if Greenland's ice sheet melted completely? Every coast on Earth would change.
It holds about 2.9 million cubic kilometers of ice.
Melted, that is enough to raise global sea level by roughly 7.3 meters.
That is about 24 feet, taller than a two-story house, on every shoreline.
It would not happen overnight. A NASA model ran to the year 3000, and the ice was gone only in the worst case.
Even if emissions fall sharply, a NASA model still loses 8 to 25 percent of the ice by 3000.

description:
What if Greenland's entire ice sheet melted?
It holds enough ice to raise sea levels about 7.3 meters, but a NASA model shows it would take centuries.
What should we run through next?
